thread:
incident-bot: Paging: prefix-cache miss spike detected in prod-us-west — hit_rate fell from ~92% to ~60% in 15m. threshold breach at 03:12 UTC. @maya is oncall.

maya: I'm in. Thanks for the ping. Can someone drop recent eviction/reconfigure logs?

jordan: digging. I see a mass invalidation event at ~03:05 from a deployment pipeline job: `deploy-service-x` called `cache:purge(pattern=\"user:*\")` — looks like an accidental wildcard.

lee: whoa. That purge command was a manual run from CI during a canary rollback. It targeted `user:*` keys by mistake.

tilly: customer impact: a subset of inference requests started rehydrating KV at higher latency. Some 5xxs reported by customers in the 03:12–03:30 window, mostly <1% of requests but high-profile tenant A saw ~3% error spike.

evan: logs: attaching snippet of prefix cache metrics and rewarm tails: ```
[03:04:58] cache.eviction.request user:* by pipeline
[03:05:01] cache.invalidate keys=~120k pattern=user:*
[03:05:20] serving.kv.miss_rate 0.38
[03:10:30] serving.kv.miss_rate 0.41
[03:15:00] serving.kv.miss_rate 0.10
```

maya: good, that matches the alert. Are we still seeing high backend load? Any paging to disk?

jordan: disks look ok. GPU backend queues spiked because models re-populated KV caches and some requests waited for prefix rewarm. Not actual OS paging but rewarm-induced latency.

tilly: mitigation timeline proposal: 1) stop further purges (CI fixed), 2) issue targeted rewarm for the top-50 prefixes for tenant A, 3) temporarily increase cache TTL to reduce churn, 4) rollout a config block in CI to prevent wildcard purges.

maya: execute step 1 done — CI job disabled. step 2 please. @jordan @lee coordinate.

jordan: kicking targeted rewarm now: `rehydrate --prefix user:tenantA --top=50` start 03:22. will monitor.

lee: adding emergency rule to block `cache:purge` with `*` in prod-runner. patch in review: https://git.redwood/repo/PR-4821

evan: quick note on hit-rate timeline: uploaded heatmap to the incident bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/2111112222/hitrate-heatmap.png

support-bot: Customer A ticket #CS-9123 flagged increased latency; auto-created postmortem stub.

maya: hypothesis tracking (in-thread): H1: accidental `user:*` purge caused broad eviction -> KV rewarms -> transient latency + errors for high-rps tenants. H2: some requests routed to cold model variants due to routing fallback, amplifying errors. H3: TTLs too low for certain prefix families causing faster regen after purge.

tilly: evidence for H1: eviction event in logs + synchronous rehydration window matches impact window. Evidence against H2: routing logs show no variant fallback during window. Evidence for H3: prefix family `user:recent` had TTL=300s, which is short.

maya: action items: - Jordan: collect full invalidation command lineage + who triggered it (audit) - Lee: land CI guard PR and confirm blocked - Evan: surface top-100 evicted prefixes and per-prefix QPS - Tilly: draft customer-facing incident message for Customer A and PLG status update

jordan: audit shows user `deploy-bot` initiated purge; owner is `ops-scripts@infra` — will follow up.

lee: CI guard PR merged 03:34, deploy blockers added.

evan: uploaded per-prefix rewarm progress CSV: s3://redwood-incidents/2111112222/rehydrate-progress.csv

support-bot: Noted. CS message drafted and sent to Customer A at 03:40: "We're investigating an increased latency and some errors, root cause appears to be an accidental cache purge. We're prioritizing rewarming and mitigations."

maya: cool. Closing immediate pager — monitoring for residuals for 2h. If hit_rate doesn't recover to >85% in 30m, reopen.

tilly: preliminary RCA notes to append to postmortem: - primary cause: manual wildcard purge from CI - contributing: short TTLs on hot prefix family - mitigation: CI guard, targeted rewarm tooling, TTL adjustments, alert refinement to signal wildcard purges specifically

evan: follow-up data queries planned: - span logs correlating purge -> first 5xx - per-tenant miss-rate time series - rewarm cost estimate (token and CPU/GPU)

maya: thanks all. I'll own the follow-up postmortem and timeline. Please drop any remaining logs or notes here.

jordan: FYI I put a `--dry-run` toggle in the rehydrate tool post-incident so we can rehearse without mass hits.

lee: question for postmortem: should we add a guard that requires 2-person auth for any `cache:purge(pattern=*)` in prod? putting proposal on RFC board.

tilly: +1 for 2-person auth for wildcard purges. also recommend a new alert rule that pairs `cache.invalidate` events with `hit_rate` drops above threshold within 10m.

maya: noted. If no objections let's capture all of this and sync tomorrow at 09:00 for RCA handoff.

support-bot: Postmortem stub: https://docs.redwood/incidents/2111112222/postmortem (auto-created)

incident-bot: Incident resolved for alert group prefix-cache-miss-prod-us-west. status: mitigated -> monitoring.
